'''Dairis Bertāns''' (born 9 September 1989) is a Latvian professional [[basketball]] player for [[Dubai Basketball]] of the [[ABA League]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. Bertāns also plays for the [[Latvia national basketball team]]. He is the older brother of [[Dāvis Bertāns]]. He is a {{convert|6|ft|4|in|adj=on}}, {{convert|200|lb|adj=on}} [[shooting guard]].

==Professional career==
===Latvia (2004–2013)===
From 2004 to 2006, Bertāns played for [[BK Valmiera|Valmiera]] and its junior team. In 2006, he signed with [[ASK Rīga]]. In 2006–07, he played for ASK Rīga's junior team, and in 2007–08, he made his debut for the senior squad.

In March 2009, he left ASK Rīga following the club's financial difficulties and signed a two-year deal with [[BK Ventspils|Ventspils]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Carchia |first=E. |date=12 March 2009 |title=Hot day in Latvia |url=http://archive.sportando.basketball/en/europe/latvia/75556/hot-day-in-latvia.html |access-date=2 March 2019 |work=Sportando.basketball}}</ref>

In August 2010, he signed a two-year deal with [[BK VEF Rīga|VEF Rīga]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Carchia |first=E. |date=10 August 2010 |title=VEF Riga announce Valters, Grafs and Bertans |url=http://archive.sportando.basketball/en/europe/latvia/84008/vef-riga-announce-valters-grafs-and-bertans.html |access-date=2 March 2019 |work=Sportando.basketball}}</ref> VEF Rīga's coach at the time, [[Rimas Kurtinaitis]], saw potential in Bertāns as a point guard despite primarily being a shooting guard. So, during the 2010–11 season, Bertāns developed [[point guard]] skills to a different level, and was one of the key factors in VEF Rīga's first championship.

In July 2012, he re-signed with VEF Rīga on a three-year deal.<ref>{{cite web |last=Carchia |first=E. |date=12 July 2012 |title=VEF Riga keeps Dairis Bertans |url=http://archive.sportando.basketball/en/europe/latvia/93426/vef-riga-keeps-dairis-bertans.html |access-date=2 March 2019 |work=Sportando.basketball}}</ref>

===Bilbao Basket (2013–2016)===
In June 2013, Bertāns parted ways with VEF Rīga to sign a three-year deal with [[Bilbao Basket]] of the [[Liga ACB]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Carchia |first=E. |date=6 June 2013 |title=Bilbao signs Dairis Bertans to a three-year deal |url=http://archive.sportando.basketball/en/europe/spain/101739/bilbao-signs-dairis-bertans-to-a-three-year-deal.html |access-date=2 March 2019 |work=Sportando.basketball}}</ref> In one of his first games with Bilbao, he scored 19 points in a preseason game against the [[2013–14 Philadelphia 76ers season|Philadelphia 76ers]] of the [[NBA]].<ref>{{cite web |date=6 October 2013 |title=76ers 106, Bilbao Basket 104 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400491498 |access-date=22 January 2024 |work=ESPN.com}}</ref>

In July 2014, Bertāns joined the [[2014–15 Boston Celtics season|Boston Celtics]] for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite news |date=1 July 2014 |title=Celtics Announce 2014 Orlando Summer League Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/celtics-announce-2014-summer-league-roster |access-date=22 January 2024 |work=NBA.com}}</ref>

In his second season with Bilbao, Bertāns helped the team to reach the [[2015 ACB Playoffs]] as the fifth seed, but they eventually lost to [[Valencia Basket|Valencia]] in the quarterfinals.

In July 2015, Bertāns joined the [[2015–16 San Antonio Spurs season|San Antonio Spurs]] for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]]. He averaged 11.3 points, 3 rebounds and 1.6 in three games played for the Spurs.<ref>{{cite web |last=Julian |first=M. |date=3 July 2015 |title=Spurs Announce 2015 Summer League Rosters for Utah & Las Vegas |url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-announce-2015-summer-league-rosters-utah-las-vegas |access-date=2 March 2019 |work=NBA.com}}</ref>

On 20 January 2016, Bertāns recorded a season-high 27 points, shooting 6-of-11 from three-point range, along with four rebounds and two assists in a 76–78 loss to [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|Bayern Munich]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Dominion Bilbao Basket vs. FC Bayern Munich - Game | url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/eurocup/game-center/?seasoncode=U2015&gamecode=213 | work=EuroCupBasketball.com | date=20 January 2016 | access-date=2 March 2019}}</ref>

===Darüşşafaka (2016–2017)===
On 13 July 2016, Bertāns signed a 1+1-year deal with Turkish club [[Darüşşafaka Doğuş]] under head coach [[David Blatt]].<ref>{{cite news |date=13 July 2016 |title=Darussafaka Dogus lands Dairis Bertans |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/206151/darussafaka-dogus-lands-dairis-bertans.html |access-date=16 July 2016 |work=Sportando.com |archive-date=16 July 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160716071933/http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/206151/darussafaka-dogus-lands-dairis-bertans.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> On 12 January 2017, Bertāns recorded a career-high 29 points, shooting 10-of-13 from the field, along with five assists in a 98–89 win over [[Saski Baskonia|Baskonia]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Darussafaka Dogus Istanbul vs. Baskonia Vitoria Gasteiz - Game|url=https://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=130&seasoncode=E2016 |access-date=1 March 2019|work=EuroLeague.net|date=12 January 2017}}</ref> Bertāns helped the team to reach the [[2017 EuroLeague Playoffs]] as the eighth seed, but they eventually were eliminated by [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] in the quarterfinals.

===Olimpia Milano (2017–2019)===
[[File:Dairis Bertāns 45 AX Armani Exchange Olimpia Milan 20171130.jpg|150px|thumb|Bertāns with Olimpia Milano in November 2017]]
On 10 July 2017, Bertāns signed with Italian club [[Olimpia Milano]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Mariani |first=Ivan |date=10 July 2017 |title=Olimpia adds three-point shooter Dairis Bertans |url=https://www.olimpiamilano.com/en/olimpia-adds-three-point-shooter-dairis-bertans |access-date=22 January 2024 |work=Olimpiamilano.com}}</ref> In his first season with Milano, Bertāns helped Milano to win the [[2017–18 LBA season|2018 Italian League]] championship.

On 29 June 2018, Bertāns re-signed with Milano for the 2018–19 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Olimpia Milano keeps Dairis Bertans|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/italy/serie-a/279335/olimpia-milano-keeps-dairis-bertans.html|access-date=29 June 2018|work=sportando.basketball|date=29 June 2018}}{{Dead link|date=August 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> However, on 1 March 2019, Bertāns parted ways with Milano so he can continue the season in the NBA.<ref>{{cite news |last=Carchia |first=Emiliano |date=1 March 2019 |title=Bertans: Olimpia gave me the opportunity to realize a dream that I was pursuing since I was a kid |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/bertans-olimpia-gave-me-the-opportunity-to-realize-a-dream-that-i-was-pursuing-since-i-was-a-kid/ |access-date=1 March 2019 |work=sportando.basketball}}</ref>

===New Orleans Pelicans (2019)===
On 2 March 2019, Bertāns signed with the [[2018–19 New Orleans Pelicans season|New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite news|title=New Orleans Pelicans sign Dairis Bertans | url=https://www.nba.com/article/2019/03/02/pelicans-sign-dairis-bertans-official-release | access-date=3 March 2019 | work=NBA.com |date=2 March 2019}}</ref> Bertāns later made his NBA debut eight days later, recording just one assist in six minutes of action in a 128–116 loss to the [[2018–19 Atlanta Hawks season|Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pelicans – Hawks |url=https://www.nba.com/games/20190310/NOPATL#/boxscore |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200813122223/https://www.nba.com/games/20190310/NOPATL#/boxscore |archive-date=13 August 2020 |access-date=16 March 2019 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> He then recorded a rebound two days later in a 130–113 loss to the [[2018–19 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bucks – Pelicans |url=https://www.nba.com/games/20190312/MILNOP#/boxscore |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181226015211/http://www.nba.com/games/20190312/MILNOP#/boxscore |archive-date=26 December 2018 |access-date=16 March 2019 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> Bertāns made his first basket with a three-pointer in a 138–136 overtime loss to the [[2018–19 Phoenix Suns season|Phoenix Suns]] on 16 March.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Suns – Pelicans |url=https://www.nba.com/games/20190316/PHXNOP#/boxscore |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200917013316/https://www.nba.com/games/20190316/PHXNOP#/boxscore |archive-date=17 September 2020 |access-date=17 March 2019 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On 7 July 2019, he was waived by the Pelicans.<ref>{{cite web |last=Crum |first=Clark |date=7 July 2019 |title=Pelicans Waive Dairis Bertans |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2019/07/pelicans-to-waive-dairis-bertans.html |access-date=13 July 2019 |work=hoopsrumors.com}}</ref>

===Khimki (2019–2021)===
On 8 July 2019, Bertāns signed a two-year contract with [[BC Khimki|Khimki]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Khimki inks shooting ace Bertans for two years|url=https://www.euroleague.net/news/i/9scmooige9dcck7w|date=8 July 2019|website=euroleague.net|access-date=13 July 2019}}</ref> reuniting with head coach [[Rimas Kurtinaitis]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Khimki, Kurtinaitis together until 2021|url=https://www.euroleague.net/news/i/9s5qfs97a3teo6ka/khimki-kurtinaitis-together-until-2021|date=5 July 2019|website=euroleague.net|access-date=28 August 2020}}</ref> He played in 21 out of 28 [[Euroleague]] games<ref>{{cite web|title=EuroLeague 2019-20 STATISTICS|url=https://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=000436&seasoncode=E2019|date=28 August 2020|website=euroleague.net|access-date=28 August 2020}}</ref> and BC Khimki won 13 games, placing them 7th place in the standings,<ref>{{cite web|title= Standings|url=https://www.euroleague.net/main/standings?seasoncode=E2019|date=28 August 2020|website=euroleague.net|access-date=28 August 2020}}</ref> which would qualify the team to [[playoff]]s. On 25 May 2020, Euroleague Basketball cancelled its competitions due to the COVID-19 pandemic.<ref>{{cite news |title=ECA Shareholders Executive Board announces decisions regarding 2019-20 and 2020-21 seasons |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague-basketball/news/i/am9neim7ahpbaqym |access-date=25 May 2020 |work=[[Euroleague Basketball]] |date=25 May 2020 |archive-date=3 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200603141747/https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague-basketball/news/i/am9neim7ahpbaqym |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Real Betis (2021–2023)===
On 27 July 2021, Bertāns signed with [[Real Betis Baloncesto|Real Betis]] of the [[Liga ACB]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Carchia |first=Emiliano |date=27 July 2021 |title=Dairis Bertans inks with Coosur Real Betis |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/dairis-bertans-inks-with-coosur-real-betis/ |access-date=27 July 2021 |website=Sportando}}</ref>

===Return to VEF Rīga (2023–present)===
On 14 July 2023, it was announced that after ten years away from home, Bertāns had returned to [[BK VEF Rīga|VEF Rīga]], signing a two-year contract.<ref>{{cite web |last=Dilāns |first=Kristiāns |date=14 July 2023 |title=Izlases kapteinis Dairis Bertāns pēc desmit gadiem atgriežas dzimtenē un pastiprina VEF |url=https://sportacentrs.com/basketbols/lbl/14072023-izlases_kapteinis_dairis_bertans_pec_desm |access-date=22 January 2024 |website=sportacentrs.com |language=lv}}</ref>

==National team career==
Bertāns has been member of the Latvian U-16, U-19 and U-20 national teams, as well as the senior national team. He led Latvia to a bronze medal at the 2007 [[FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship|U18 European Championship]] in Madrid, Spain. He has since represented the [[Latvia men's national basketball team|Latvia national team]] at the [[EuroBasket 2011]]. Furthermore, he was also the leading scorer (14.1 ppg) for Latvia in 2012, when he helped Latvia earn a spot in [[EuroBasket 2013]].

Bertāns was a key player for Latvia during [[EuroBasket 2013]] where he averaged 10.9 ppg. In his best game of the tournament Bertāns had a 28-point performance against France, the eventual champions.<ref>{{cite news | title=Latvia 91 at France 102 | url=https://basketball.realgm.com/national/boxscore/2013-09-13/Latvia-at-France/140747 | access-date=1 March 2019 | work=RealGM.com | date=13 September 2013}}</ref>

He returned for [[EuroBasket 2015]] and [[EuroBasket 2017|2017]], helping Latvia get to the quarterfinal round on both occasions.

==Personal life==
{{BLP unreferenced section|date=January 2025}}
Bertāns' brother, [[Dāvis Bertāns|Dāvis]], is also a professional basketball player. Their father, [[Dainis Bertāns|Dainis]], was a professional basketball player and is currently a youth coach. Their mother is a sports teacher and a former high-level rower. During his childhood, Bertāns was raised in Latvia's northernmost town, [[Rūjiena]], until his parents moved to the capital city, [[Riga]].
